headline: 18.4 billion e-payments in 2025, yet 63% of non-urban Malaysians used cash daily in a 2021 survey
context: BNM Annual Report 2025 confirms 18.4 billion e-payment transactions and RM831 billion retail value. PayNet's late-2021 survey found 36.2% of urban and 63.5% of non-urban Malaysians used cash daily. BNM says about 95% of online fraud cases are authorised transactions.

cards.big: 18.4 billion e-payment transactions in 2025, about 538 per Malaysian. The headline growth is real. The framing of the divide is not.
cards.sub: BNM AR 2025: e-payments up 25%, retail value RM831 billion, DuitNow QR doubled to 3 billion. PayNet (late 2021): 48.4% of Malaysians paid daily expenses in cash.

cards.big: DuitNow QR doubled to 3 billion transactions in 2025 with nearly 3 million touchpoints. Average e-money transaction size rose to RM43 from RM33.
cards.sub: BNM AR 2024: DuitNow QR merchant payments worth RM31.1 billion over 2024. ReDI signed up 22,368 small traders by May 2025.

cards.big: PayNet's late-2021 survey found 36.2% of urban and 63.5% of non-urban Malaysians used cash daily. BNM's Basic Banking policy keeps cash services for basic accounts.
cards.sub: BNM Financial Inclusion Framework 2023-26: cash reliance persists among low-income, elderly and rural users. Sarawak runs S Pay Global.

cards.big: RM2.8B is the 2025 scam impact across all channels, not e-wallet fraud. Banks blocked about RM1.2B of fraudulent transactions.
cards.sub: BNM: unauthorised cases eased in 1H 2025, then malware-driven transfers rose. NSRC took 146,167 calls, kept RM34.05M from syndicates and returned RM6.65M to victims.

cards.big: The real question is not how fast we reach 100% cashless. It is who gets left without working alternatives when the cash window closes.
Malaysia has the rails. The next decade is about whether consumer protection catches up before more vulnerable users are pushed onto a system that cannot protect them.
